items.title: Joe Darensbourg and Minor "Ram" Hall Interview, 1957-04-18
items.q: I worked with Jelly Roll for a couple of weeks, he came through there.

ctx.x: Yeah. No, I figured that out myself. What was it, tennis? No, Aldo. Aldo.

The first time I picked up a saxophone, I could play it. Oh yeah? Yeah. But, also singing is quite different. From a clarinet? Yeah. Well, all, all saxophones, things are the same for that matter. But, uh, it's different from a clarinet. Still in all, if you can play a clarinet, you can play a saxophone. Something real easy, because the clarinet is a lot more difficult instrument than a saxophone. But I had, uh, and I had food with a saxophone before, a little bit, you know, because my teacher was a saxophone…
Joe Poston? Yeah. Just playing with Jimmy New York? He was playing saxophone. Yeah? Yeah.

items.title: 63477_Joe Darensbourg oral history interview
items.q: when I played with Jelly Roll for two weeks, I don't remember nobody who was in that band.

ctx.x: You weren't that familiar with Dewey Jackson's band, then. You didn't see much of them.

No. I missed a lot of those things. For the first thing... Like, when I played with Jelly Roll for two weeks, I don't remember nobody who was in that band. I did a lot of drinking, and I didn't pay no attention to who I was playing next to. Just so I got paid.
Well, it seems like most of the New Orleans guys that traveled, that came up the river or did whatever, they didn't leave the same way as you. I mean, you left on a medicine show and went around...
